title: Timers: create, schedule, edit, rename, delete (ODC) and create with Action/Description (O11); the ODC schedule tree is derived

capabilities.title: Timers (scheduled server actions): create, point at an action, schedule, edit, rename, delete
capabilities.summary: ITimer under the module with Action = IServerAction:<Name> and Description; TimeoutInMinutes and Priority exist on both lanes. ODC also has CronSchedule (five fields) and a derived child ScheduleConfiguration (ISchedule with typed ScheduleItems) rebuilt when the timer's CronSchedule or Schedule changes; O11 has the Schedule text instead, as the Service Studio writes it: "00:00 01:00 02:00 03:00 04:00 05:00 06:00 07:00 08:00 09:00 10:00 11:00 12:00 13:00 14:00 15:00 16:00 17:00 18:00 19:00 20:00 21:00 22:00 23:00", "00:00", "00:05 Mon" (pacote-laneE-timer-schedule). No O11 job writes TimeoutInMinutes or Priority.

route.operation: create ITimer @espace; set Action IServerAction:<Name>; set Description; O11: set Schedule "00:00 01:00 02:00 03:00 04:00 05:00 06:00 07:00 08:00 09:00 10:00 11:00 12:00 13:00 14:00 15:00 16:00 17:00 18:00 19:00 20:00 21:00 22:00 23:00" | "00:00" | "00:05 Mon"; ODC: set CronSchedule "m h dom mon dow" (or Schedule), TimeoutInMinutes, Priority; deliver with o11_deliver / studio_deliver

capabilities.guidance: The scheduled logic is a server action (front A): create it first or point at an existing one (set Action IServerAction:<Name>). ODC: a timer counts as a consumer of its action, so deleting the timer leaves the action without consumers (UnusedUserAction, declared in timer-lifecycle); on O11 usages is not proven. ODC: change the schedule through the PARENT (CronSchedule or Schedule on the timer); the schedule values in ScheduleConfiguration and its items are derived and read-only, while ScheduleConfiguration.WhenPublished and the items' Interval are writable but untested. Read the tree by path ITimer:<T>/ScheduleConfiguration/#IMinute, #IHour, #IDayOfWeek; the item count depends on the route (CronSchedule builds five items including Any placeholders, Schedule "07:45" builds two), so never infer the schedule from the count. A six-field cron is not accepted on ODC. O11: the schedule is the Schedule text ("00:00 01:00 02:00 03:00 04:00 05:00 06:00 07:00 08:00 09:00 10:00 11:00 12:00 13:00 14:00 15:00 16:00 17:00 18:00 19:00 20:00 21:00 22:00 23:00", "00:00", "00:05 Mon"), read back by get.

read.route: get/dump ITimer:<Timer>; ODC schedule tree by path ITimer:<Timer>/ScheduleConfiguration/#IMinute|#IHour|#IDayOfWeek

odc.scope: Action, Description, CronSchedule, Schedule, TimeoutInMinutes and the derived ScheduleConfiguration read back before and after each change

o11.scope: get after create and set (Action, Description, Schedule)

preconditions: the timer is a consumer of its action (usages on the action lists it)

o11.note: no O11 job runs usages on a timer

preconditions: the action to schedule exists (or is created in the same job)
ODC: CronSchedule has FIVE fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week)
ODC: the schedule tree is rebuilt from the parent; its schedule values are read-only (Interval/WhenPublished writable, untested)

odc.scope: Action, Description, CronSchedule, Schedule ("07:45"), TimeoutInMinutes, Priority; edited on a timer another job created

o11.note: no O11 job renames a timer

preconditions: the action the timer woke loses its consumer: expect UnusedUserAction unless something else calls it

odc.scope: deleted after rename; find ITimer confirms it is gone; UnusedUserAction declared

o11.note: no O11 job deletes a timer

limits.text: CronSchedule takes five fields; a six-field cron is refused.

The schedule values of ScheduleConfiguration (ISchedule) and its ScheduleItems are derived and read-only (census); only the parent's CronSchedule/Schedule changes the schedule. ISchedule.WhenPublished and IScheduleItem.Interval are writable but untested.

differences.text: Only ODC timers have CronSchedule and the derived ScheduleConfiguration tree; O11 ITimer has the Schedule string. TimeoutInMinutes and Priority exist on both lanes (writable in the O11 catalog), but no O11 job writes them.
